builder_plan.change: Change only the attention cache policy, after checking model and runtime support.

steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers
summary: LoopKV replaces uniform-bit KV cache quantization (e.g., KIVI-4) with per-(loop,layer) precision allocation—4-bit, 2-bit, or cross-loop reuse—based on an offline sensitivity profile, executed via a fused vLLM kernel. Costs include a one-time offline profiling step, a custom fused kernel, and plan storage; it applies only to looped transformers that keep separate KV per loop, such as Ouro. It can fail if damage-additivity assumptions break on other models or workloads, if skipping low-attention values compounds errors across loops, or if the target deployment does not use looped architectures at all.
rationale: The method is specialized to looped transformers like Ouro, which the reader is unlikely to be serving, so the technique is worth tracking but not adopting unless such a model enters production.

claims.statement: LoopKV replaces uniform-bit KV cache quantization (e.g., KIVI-4) with per-(loop,layer) precision allocation—4-bit, 2-bit, or cross-loop reuse—based on an offline sensitivity profile, executed via a fused vLLM kernel. Costs include a one-time offline profiling step, a custom fused kernel, and plan storage; it applies only to looped transformers that keep separate KV per loop, such as Ouro. It can fail if damage-additivity assumptions break on other models or workloads, if skipping low-attention values compounds errors across loops, or if the target deployment does not use looped architectures at all.
Sustains 1.7-2.2x KIVI-4's goodput under a latency SLO with 16K-token maximum length, storing 35% less KV than uniform 4-bit quantization.
